correctness.rationale: In three rounds Duplicator needs at most three leaves in any visited star and at most three fresh components of each type. Matching components consistently preserves equality, within-component adjacency, and nonadjacency between components, including when a previously marked vertex is chosen again. This proves truncation for all nonempty finite star forests and never increases the order of a representative. The iterated sets of six-bit ordered triple types are the exact extension invariants of the three-round game: atomic types decide the final position, and equality of extension sets is precisely the back-and-forth response condition at each earlier position. Nonemptiness allows each partial atomic type to be recovered from an extension. An independent direct minimax classification in increasing order of the 255 profiles gives 22 classes and one representative minimum nine, for profile (0,0,3,0), with all 231 pairs of representatives inequivalent. Size-monotone truncation excludes any smaller noncanonical witness.
residual_risks: The census is exact over the finite reduction; it is the symbolic game argument that extends it to arbitrarily large finite stars and forests. The nine-vertex uniqueness is a uniqueness of the class requiring that minimum, not a claim about all graph realizations.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A linear forest with a dominating vertex must be P1, P2 or P3. The rank-three assertion that there are at least three vertices leaves only P3. In P3 two distinct nonadjacent vertices together dominate; in S3 no such pair does. This, too, is rank three. Thus the linear-forest census cannot simply be restricted or reused as an enumeration of every star-forest type.

value.rationale: This is an exact low-rank model classification for a natural class of forests, with no expansion of the language or artificial vertex cutoff. Rank three is the first rank that can witness two distinct neighbors of a vertex. A sharp uniform representative bound and its extremal class give a useful finite domain for deciding equivalence at that depth; the computation identifies what the general finite-type theorem cannot supply.
residual_risks: It does not classify larger rank, arbitrary forests, or counting logic; no such extrapolation is needed for the finite representative result.
